title: Idempotent token fencing and attribution-safelist mapper for cross-region retries
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Production incidents over the last two months exposed a small but material class of double-counting when requests are retried from edge proxies across regions. Root cause: transient downstream failures plus non-idempotent attribution joins allow duplicate accounting rows to be produced during asynchronous ingestion. This ticket implements a two-part fix: (1) a lightweight token fencing layer in the ingestion gateway that enforces a short-lived idempotency window keyed by request fingerprint + region, and (2) an attribution-safelist mapper that canonicalizes ambiguous route/variant labels before they reach the billing joiner.

Problem details:
- Symptom: customers observed occasional 1-3% over-billing for high-throughput routes during regional failovers.
- Path: edge retry -> alternative region -> ingestion service accepts retry as distinct because of per-hop metadata mutations (route labels, tenant sharding headers) -> downstream joiner produces duplicate attribution entries for the same logical request.
- Frequency: ~0.02% of tokens across global traffic during peak hours, but concentrated on multi-region failover windows.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
1) Eliminate duplicate attribution for retried requests within a 60s idempotency window for the same logical request fingerprint (measured by unique request_token + initial call timestamp tolerance).
2) Ensure attribution-safelist mapper reduces label cardinality by mapping noisy labels (edge-probe, legacy-route, region-override) into canonical route names used by billing joiner.
3) Introduce a telemetry dashboard showing pre/post duplicate-rate, ingestion idempotency hits, and per-route token delta. Baseline: duplicate-rate <= 0.001% of tokens in steady state.
4) Rollbackable rollout with feature flag and canary across 3 regions.

Design notes:
- Ingestion gateway (ingest-proxy) will maintain an in-memory LRU for recent request_fingerprints with a write-through to a compact Redis hash for cross-instance lookups in failover. Entries expire after 60s + clock skew padding. This keeps per-instance memory small while enabling cross-instance idempotency during multi-instance ingress.
- Request fingerprint = sha256(tenant_id + request_id + model_signature + first_seen_unix_floor(5s)). We tolerate minor clock skew by floor binning first_seen to 5s buckets.
- Attribution safelist mapper lives in the attribution preprocessor microservice: configuration-driven mapping file in S3/ConfigStore (yaml) that maps variant labels to canonical_route with precedence rules. The mapper will log unmapped labels to a low-sample error sink for follow-up.
- Downstream billing joiner will be updated to rely on canonical_route and idempotency markers when merging events. The joiner will continue to support legacy labels for 30 days of migration.

Data migration and compatibility:
- New accounting rows include a new column: idempotency_token and canonical_route. These are backfilled for 7 days of buffered events during the rollout window. Historical reports are unaffected; we will keep a compatibility view that projects canonical_route where missing.

Operational plan and rollout:
1) Implement ingest-proxy idempotency in feature-flagged mode (FF: ingest.idempotency) behind a config guard. Unit tests + chaos injection.
2) Deploy attribution-safelist mapper to staging; sync canonical mappings from sales/PM-approved mapping doc in Drive.
3) Canary step: enable in eu-west-1 for 24 hours with shadow writes to billing-test dataset. Monitor duplicate-rate, idempotency_hits, Redis miss-rate, and tail-latency.
4) Gradual rollout to remaining regions over 72 hours with automated rollback if duplicate-rate increases or any latency SLOs degrade beyond 10th percentile thresholds.

Metrics to track:
- duplicate_token_rate (pre/post), idempotency_hit_ratio, redis_miss_ratio, ingestion_99p_latency, per-route token delta, unmapped_label_count.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.com/confluence/display/BILL/Idempotency+and+Safelist+Mapper+Design
- Mapping spreadsheet (PM-owned): https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AbcExample
- Staging PR (ingest-proxy): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/418
- Billing joiner PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-joiner/pull/223

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: redis cross-region latency introduces false negatives -> mitigation: local LRU as primary and async best-effort cross-check; tune TTL conservatively.
- Risk: canonicalization mis-maps a route causing broad attribution shifts -> mitigation: low-sample rollouts and unmapped_label alerting + fast rollback.

Next steps (short-term):
- Spike: prototype fingerprinting and measure fingerprint collision rate on 24h traffic sample (assigned to Diego).
- PM to finalize mapping sheet and mark 3 pilot routes (auth, embeddings, chat-completions) for canary.
